title.ar: تفاضل وتكامل المتجهات ونظريات غرين وستوكس

body.en: The capstone of multivariable calculus integrates vector fields—assignments of directed force, flow, or field vectors to every spatial point—along paths and across surfaces. Connecting line and surface integrals to internal differential operators (\( abla f\), \( abla \cdot \mathbf{F}\), \( abla imes \mathbf{F}\)), the fundamental theorems of vector calculus (Green's, Stokes', and the Divergence Theorem) unify physical conservation laws across dimensions.
body.ar: The capstone of multivariable التفاضل والتكامل integrates vector fields—assignments of directed force, flow, or field المتجهات to every spatial point—along paths and across surfaces. Connecting line and surface التكاملات to internal differential operators (\( abla f\), \( abla \cdot \mathbf{F}\), \( abla imes \mathbf{F}\)), the fundamental theorems of المتجه التفاضل والتكامل (Green's, Stokes', and the Divergence مبرهنة) unify physical conservation laws across dimensions.

label.en: ● Definition 15.1 — Vector Fields, Line Integrals & Work
label.ar: ● تعريف 15.1 — المتجه Fields, Line التكاملات & Work

body.en:
A vector field on \(\mathbb{R}^3\) is a mapping \(\mathbf{F}(x, y, z) = P\mathbf{i} + Q\mathbf{j} + R\mathbf{k}\). If \(C\) is a smooth curve parameterized by \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) for \(a \le t \le b\), the line integral of \(\mathbf{F}\) along \(C\) (representing physical work done by \(\mathbf{F}\) on a moving particle) is:

\[ \int_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = \int_a^b \mathbf{F}\big(\mathbf{r}(t)\big) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t)\,dt = \int_C (P\,dx + Q\,dy + R\,dz) \]

A vector field is conservative if there exists a scalar potential function \(f\) such that \(\mathbf{F} = \nabla f\).
body.ar:
A vector field on \(\mathbb{R}^3\) is a mapping \(\mathbf{F}(x, y, z) = P\mathbf{i} + Q\mathbf{j} + R\mathbf{k}\). If \(C\) is a smooth curve parameterized by \(\mathbf{r}(t)\) for \(a \le t \le b\), the line التكامل of \(\mathbf{F}\) along \(C\) (representing physical work done by \(\mathbf{F}\) on a moving particle) is:

\[ \int_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = \int_a^b \mathbf{F}\big(\mathbf{r}(t)\big) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t)\,dt = \int_C (P\,dx + Q\,dy + R\,dz) \]

A المتجه field is conservative if there exists a scalar potential الدالة \(f\) such that \(\mathbf{F} = \nabla f\).

label.en: ▲ Theorem 15.1 — Fundamental Theorem for Line Integrals (The Gradient Theorem)
label.ar: ▲ مبرهنة 15.1 — Fundamental مبرهنة for Line التكاملات (The Gradient مبرهنة)

body.en:
Let \(C\) be a piecewise-smooth curve from initial point \(A = \mathbf{r}(a)\) to terminal point \(B = \mathbf{r}(b)\). If \(f\) is a continuously differentiable scalar function, then:

\[ \int_C abla f \cdot d\mathbf{r} = f(B) - f(A) = f ig(\mathbf{r}(b) ig) - f ig(\mathbf{r}(a) ig) \]

Fundamental Consequences of Path Independence:

  • Path Independence: The work done depends only on the endpoints \(A\) and \(B\), completely independent of the specific trajectory taken.
  • Zero Closed-Loop Circulation: For any closed path \(C\) (where \(A = B\)):
    \[ \oint_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = 0 \]
  • Curl Test on Simply Connected Domains: A field \(\mathbf{F}\) with continuous derivatives on a simply connected domain is conservative if and only if \( abla imes \mathbf{F} = \mathbf{0}\) (in 2D: \( rac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = rac{\partial P}{\partial y}\)).

Analytical Proof via Multivariable Chain Rule

Let \(C\) be parameterized by \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \langle x(t), y(t), z(t) angle\) for \(a \le t \le b\). By definition of the line integral:

\[ \int_C abla f \cdot d\mathbf{r} = \int_a^b abla f ig(\mathbf{r}(t) ig) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t)\,dt \]\[ = \int_a^b \left( rac{\partial f}{\partial x} rac{dx}{dt} + rac{\partial f}{\partial y} rac{dy}{dt} + rac{\partial f}{\partial z} rac{dz}{dt} ight) dt \]

By the Multivariable Chain Rule, the integrand inside the parentheses is precisely the total time derivative \( rac{d}{dt} ig[f(\mathbf{r}(t)) ig]\):

\[ \int_a^b abla f ig(\mathbf{r}(t) ig) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t)\,dt = \int_a^b rac{d}{dt} ig[f(\mathbf{r}(t)) ig]\,dt \]

By the single-variable Fundamental Theorem of Calculus, integrating a derivative yields the net evaluation at boundary points:

\[ \int_a^b rac{d}{dt} ig[f(\mathbf{r}(t)) ig]\,dt = \Big[ f ig(\mathbf{r}(t) ig) \Big]_a^b = f ig(\mathbf{r}(b) ig) - f ig(\mathbf{r}(a) ig) = f(B) - f(A) \quad lacksquare \]
body.ar:
Let \(C\) be a piecewise-smooth curve from initial point \(A = \mathbf{r}(a)\) to terminal point \(B = \mathbf{r}(b)\). If \(f\) is a continuously differentiable scalar الدالة, then:

\[ \int_C abla f \cdot d\mathbf{r} = f(B) - f(A) = f ig(\mathbf{r}(b) ig) - f ig(\mathbf{r}(a) ig) \]

Fundamental Consequences of Path Independence:

  • Path Independence: The work done depends only on the endpoints \(A\) and \(B\), completely independent of the specific trajectory taken.
  • Zero Closed-Loop Circulation: For any closed path \(C\) (حيث \(A = B\)):
    \[ \oint_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = 0 \]
  • Curl Test on Simply Connected Domains: A field \(\mathbf{F}\) with continuous المشتقات on a simply connected المجال is conservative if and only if \( abla imes \mathbf{F} = \mathbf{0}\) (in 2D: \( rac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = rac{\partial P}{\partial y}\)).

Analytical برهان via Multivariable Chain Rule

Let \(C\) be parameterized by \(\mathbf{r}(t) = \langle x(t), y(t), z(t) angle\) for \(a \le t \le b\). By definition of the line التكامل:

\[ \int_C abla f \cdot d\mathbf{r} = \int_a^b abla f ig(\mathbf{r}(t) ig) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t)\,dt \]\[ = \int_a^b \left( rac{\partial f}{\partial x} rac{dx}{dt} + rac{\partial f}{\partial y} rac{dy}{dt} + rac{\partial f}{\partial z} rac{dz}{dt} ight) dt \]

By the Multivariable Chain Rule, the integrand inside the parentheses is precisely the total time المشتقة \( rac{d}{dt} ig[f(\mathbf{r}(t)) ig]\):

\[ \int_a^b abla f ig(\mathbf{r}(t) ig) \cdot \mathbf{r}'(t)\,dt = \int_a^b rac{d}{dt} ig[f(\mathbf{r}(t)) ig]\,dt \]

By the single-المتغير Fundamental مبرهنة of التفاضل والتكامل, integrating a المشتقة yields the net evaluation at boundary points:

\[ \int_a^b rac{d}{dt} ig[f(\mathbf{r}(t)) ig]\,dt = \Big[ f ig(\mathbf{r}(t) ig) \Big]_a^b = f ig(\mathbf{r}(b) ig) - f ig(\mathbf{r}(a) ig) = f(B) - f(A) \quad lacksquare \]

label.en: ◆ Why It Works — First-Principles Derivation (Vector Calculus)
label.ar: ◆ لماذا تعمل هذه الطريقة رياضياً — First-Principles اشتقاق (المتجه التفاضل والتكامل)

body.en:
Why Orthogonal Projection & Eigenvalue Characteristic Equations Work: Decompose \(\mathbf{u} = c\mathbf{v} + \mathbf{w}\) where \(\mathbf{w} \perp \mathbf{v}\). Taking the dot product with \(\mathbf{v}\) uses \(\mathbf{w}\cdot\mathbf{v} = 0\) to isolate \(c\):

\[ \mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v} = c(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{v}) + 0 \implies c = \frac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{\|\mathbf{v}\|^2} \]

For eigenvalues, \(A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}\) with \(\mathbf{v} \ne \mathbf{0}\) is equivalent to \((A - \lambda I)\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{0}\). A homogeneous linear system has a non-trivial nullspace vector \(\mathbf{v} \ne \mathbf{0}\) if and only if the matrix \(A - \lambda I\) is singular, yielding the characteristic polynomial \(\det(A - \lambda I) = 0\).
body.ar:
Why Orthogonal Projection & Eigenvalue Characteristic المعادلات Work: Decompose \(\mathbf{u} = c\mathbf{v} + \mathbf{w}\) حيث \(\mathbf{w} \perp \mathbf{v}\). Taking the dot product with \(\mathbf{v}\) uses \(\mathbf{w}\cdot\mathbf{v} = 0\) to isolate \(c\):

\[ \mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v} = c(\mathbf{v}\cdot\mathbf{v}) + 0 \implies c = \frac{\mathbf{u}\cdot\mathbf{v}}{\|\mathbf{v}\|^2} \]

For القيم الذاتية, \(A\mathbf{v} = \lambda\mathbf{v}\) with \(\mathbf{v} \ne \mathbf{0}\) is equivalent to \((A - \lambda I)\mathbf{v} = \mathbf{0}\). A homogeneous linear system has a non-trivial nullspace المتجه \(\mathbf{v} \ne \mathbf{0}\) if and only if the المصفوفة \(A - \lambda I\) is singular, yielding the characteristic كثيرة الحدود \(\det(A - \lambda I) = 0\).

label.en: Worked Example 15.1 — Foundations: Conservative Field Work & Potential Function
label.ar: مثال محلول 15.1 — Foundations: Conservative Field Work & Potential الدالة

body.en:
Show that \(\mathbf{F}(x, y) = \langle 2xy + 3, x^2 - 4y \rangle\) is conservative, find its scalar potential function \(f(x, y)\), and compute the work done moving a particle along any path from \(A(1, 0)\) to \(B(2, 3)\).

Step 1: Verify the cross-derivative test.
\(P = 2xy + 3 \implies \frac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 2x\)
\(Q = x^2 - 4y \implies \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = 2x\)
Since \(\frac{\partial P}{\partial y} = \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}\) on all of \(\mathbb{R}^2\), \(\mathbf{F}\) is conservative.

Step 2: Construct potential function \(f(x, y)\).
Integrate \(f_x = 2xy + 3\) with respect to \(x\):

\[ f(x, y) = \int (2xy + 3)\,dx = x^2 y + 3x + g(y) \]

Differentiate with respect to \(y\) and set equal to \(Q\):

\[ f_y = x^2 + g'(y) = x^2 - 4y \implies g'(y) = -4y \implies g(y) = -2y^2 + C \]\[ f(x, y) = x^2 y + 3x - 2y^2 \]

Step 3: Apply the Fundamental Theorem for Line Integrals.

\[ W = \int_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = f(2, 3) - f(1, 0) = \big(2^2(3) + 3(2) - 2(3^2)\big) - \big(1^2(0) + 3(1) - 2(0)\big) \]\[ = (12 + 6 - 18) - (0 + 3 - 0) = 0 - 3 = -3 \]
body.ar:
Show that \(\mathbf{F}(x, y) = \langle 2xy + 3, x^2 - 4y \rangle\) is conservative, find its scalar potential الدالة \(f(x, y)\), and compute the work done moving a particle along any path from \(A(1, 0)\) to \(B(2, 3)\).

Step 1: Verify the cross-المشتقة test.
\(P = 2xy + 3 \implies \frac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 2x\)
\(Q = x^2 - 4y \implies \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = 2x\)
Since \(\frac{\partial P}{\partial y} = \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x}\) on all of \(\mathbb{R}^2\), \(\mathbf{F}\) is conservative.

Step 2: Construct potential الدالة \(f(x, y)\).
Integrate \(f_x = 2xy + 3\) بالنسبة إلى \(x\):

\[ f(x, y) = \int (2xy + 3)\,dx = x^2 y + 3x + g(y) \]

Differentiate بالنسبة إلى \(y\) and set equal to \(Q\):

\[ f_y = x^2 + g'(y) = x^2 - 4y \implies g'(y) = -4y \implies g(y) = -2y^2 + C \]\[ f(x, y) = x^2 y + 3x - 2y^2 \]

Step 3: Apply the Fundamental مبرهنة for Line التكاملات.

\[ W = \int_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = f(2, 3) - f(1, 0) = \big(2^2(3) + 3(2) - 2(3^2)\big) - \big(1^2(0) + 3(1) - 2(0)\big) \]\[ = (12 + 6 - 18) - (0 + 3 - 0) = 0 - 3 = -3 \]

body.en:
Problem (Medium): Evaluate \(\int \frac{1}{x\ln x}\,dx\).

Step-by-Step Solution: Let \(u = \ln x\), so \(du = \frac{1}{x}\,dx\). Substituting gives \(\int \frac{1}{u}\,du = \ln|u| + C = \ln|\ln x| + C\).
body.ar:
Problem (Medium): احسب قيمة \(\int \frac{1}{x\ln x}\,dx\).

Step-by-Step الحل: Let \(u = \ln x\), so \(du = \frac{1}{x}\,dx\). Substituting gives \(\int \frac{1}{u}\,du = \ln|u| + C = \ln|\ln x| + C\).

question.en:
Level 1 · Foundations
Evaluate the line integral \(\displaystyle \int_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r}\) for \(\mathbf{F} = \nabla(x^3 y + 2z)\) along any curve \(C\) from \((0, 0, 1)\) to \((2, 1, 3)\).
question.ar:
Level 1 · Foundations
احسب قيمة the line integral \(\displaystyle \int_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r}\) for \(\mathbf{F} = \nabla(x^3 y + 2z)\) along any curve \(C\) from \((0, 0, 1)\) to \((2, 1, 3)\).

solution.en:
The field is conservative with potential function \(f(x, y, z) = x^3 y + 2z\).
By the Fundamental Theorem for Line Integrals:
\[ \int_C \nabla f \cdot d\mathbf{r} = f(2, 1, 3) - f(0, 0, 1) \]
Evaluate at endpoints:
\(f(2, 1, 3) = 2^3(1) + 2(3) = 8 + 6 = 14\)
\(f(0, 0, 1) = 0^3(0) + 2(1) = 2\)
Therefore:
\[ \int_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = 14 - 2 = 12 \]

body.en:
Let \(C\) be a positively oriented (counterclockwise), piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in \(\mathbb{R}^2\) enclosing a region \(D\). If \(P(x, y)\) and \(Q(x, y)\) have continuous first partial derivatives on an open domain containing \(D\), then:

\[ \oint_C (P\,dx + Q\,dy) = \iint_D \left( \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y} \right) dA \]

Divergence & Flux Form: With unit outward normal \(\mathbf{n}\) and \(\mathbf{F} = \langle P, Q \rangle\):

\[ \oint_C \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n}\,ds = \iint_D (\nabla \cdot \mathbf{F})\,dA = \iint_D \left( \frac{\partial P}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial Q}{\partial y} \right) dA \]

Planar Area Computation: By choosing \(Q_x - P_y = 1\), the enclosed area of \(D\) can be computed solely from boundary line integrals:

\[ \text{Area}(D) = \oint_C x\,dy = -\oint_C y\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\oint_C (x\,dy - y\,dx) \]
body.ar:
Let \(C\) be a positively oriented (counterclockwise), piecewise-smooth, simple closed curve in \(\mathbb{R}^2\) enclosing a region \(D\). If \(P(x, y)\) and \(Q(x, y)\) have continuous first partial المشتقات on an open المجال containing \(D\), then:

\[ \oint_C (P\,dx + Q\,dy) = \iint_D \left( \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y} \right) dA \]

Divergence & Flux Form: With unit outward normal \(\mathbf{n}\) and \(\mathbf{F} = \langle P, Q \rangle\):

\[ \oint_C \mathbf{F} \cdot \mathbf{n}\,ds = \iint_D (\nabla \cdot \mathbf{F})\,dA = \iint_D \left( \frac{\partial P}{\partial x} + \frac{\partial Q}{\partial y} \right) dA \]

Planar المساحة Computation: By choosing \(Q_x - P_y = 1\), the enclosed المساحة of \(D\) can be computed solely from boundary line التكاملات:

\[ \text{Area}(D) = \oint_C x\,dy = -\oint_C y\,dx = \frac{1}{2}\oint_C (x\,dy - y\,dx) \]

label.en: Worked Example 15.2 — Medium: Green's Theorem Line Integral Evaluation
label.ar: مثال محلول 15.2 — Medium: Green's مبرهنة Line التكامل Evaluation

body.en:
Evaluate \(\displaystyle \oint_C (3y - e^x)\,dx + (7x + \sqrt{y^4 + 1})\,dy\), where \(C\) is the circle \(x^2 + y^2 = 9\) oriented counterclockwise.

Step 1: Identify \(P\) and \(Q\) and compute partials.
\(P = 3y - e^x \implies \frac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 3\)
\(Q = 7x + \sqrt{y^4 + 1} \implies \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = 7\)

Step 2: Apply Green's Theorem.

\[ \oint_C (P\,dx + Q\,dy) = \iint_D \left( \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y} \right) dA = \iint_D (7 - 3)\,dA = 4 \iint_D dA \]

Step 3: Evaluate over the enclosed disk \(D\).
The region \(D\) is a circle of radius \(R = 3\), so \(\text{Area}(D) = \pi(3^2) = 9\pi\):

\[ 4 \iint_D dA = 4(9\pi) = 36\pi \]
body.ar:
Evaluate \(\displaystyle \oint_C (3y - e^x)\,dx + (7x + \sqrt{y^4 + 1})\,dy\), حيث \(C\) is the الدائرة \(x^2 + y^2 = 9\) oriented counterclockwise.

Step 1: Identify \(P\) and \(Q\) and compute partials.
\(P = 3y - e^x \implies \frac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 3\)
\(Q = 7x + \sqrt{y^4 + 1} \implies \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = 7\)

Step 2: Apply Green's مبرهنة.

\[ \oint_C (P\,dx + Q\,dy) = \iint_D \left( \frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y} \right) dA = \iint_D (7 - 3)\,dA = 4 \iint_D dA \]

Step 3: احسب قيمة over the enclosed disk \(D\).
The region \(D\) is a الدائرة of نصف القطر \(R = 3\), so \(\text{Area}(D) = \pi(3^2) = 9\pi\):

\[ 4 \iint_D dA = 4(9\pi) = 36\pi \]

Level 2 · Medium

solution.en:
Identify components: \(P = 3y\) and \(Q = 5x\).
Compute partial derivatives: \(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} = 5\) and \(\frac{\partial P}{\partial y} = 3\).
Apply Green's Theorem:
\[ \oint_C (3y\,dx + 5x\,dy) = \iint_R \left(\frac{\partial Q}{\partial x} - \frac{\partial P}{\partial y}\right)\,dA = \iint_R (5 - 3)\,dA = 2 \iint_R dA. \]
The region \(R\) is a disk of radius \(r = 2\), so its area is \(\pi(2^2) = 4\pi\).
Therefore, \(2 \iint_R dA = 2(4\pi) = 8\pi\).

label.en: ▲ Theorem 15.3 — Stokes' Theorem & The Divergence Theorem (Gauss's Theorem)
label.ar: ▲ مبرهنة 15.3 — Stokes' مبرهنة & The Divergence مبرهنة (Gauss's مبرهنة)

body.en:
Green's Theorem generalizes into two grand higher-dimensional theorems:

Stokes' Theorem (Surface Curl to Boundary Circulation): Let \(S\) be an oriented piecewise-smooth surface bounded by a simple, closed, piecewise-smooth curve \(C = \partial S\) with positive orientation relative to normal \(\mathbf{n}\). If \(\mathbf{F}\) is continuously differentiable:

\[ \oint_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = \iint_S ( abla imes \mathbf{F}) \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \iint_S ( abla imes \mathbf{F}) \cdot \mathbf{n}\,dS \]

The Divergence Theorem (Volume Divergence to Surface Flux): Let \(E\) be a simple solid region enclosed by a closed surface \(S = \partial E\) oriented with outward unit normal \(\mathbf{n}\). Then:

\[ \iint_S \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \iiint_E ( abla \cdot \mathbf{F})\,dV \]

Fundamental Vector Identities:

  • \( abla imes ( abla f) \equiv \mathbf{0}\) (the curl of any gradient field is zero).
  • \( abla \cdot ( abla imes \mathbf{F}) \equiv 0\) (the divergence of any curl field is zero).

label.en: Worked Example 15.3 — Advanced: Divergence Theorem for Outward Net Flux
label.ar: مثال محلول 15.3 — Advanced: Divergence مبرهنة for Outward Net Flux

body.en:
Calculate the outward flux of \(\mathbf{F}(x, y, z) = \langle 2x + z^2, y^2 - x, 3z - y \rangle\) across the closed surface \(S\) bounding the cylinder \(x^2 + y^2 \le 4\) between \(z = 0\) and \(z = 3\).

Step 1: Compute divergence \(\nabla \cdot \mathbf{F}\).

\[ \nabla \cdot \mathbf{F} = \frac{\partial}{\partial x}(2x + z^2) + \frac{\partial}{\partial y}(y^2 - x) + \frac{\partial}{\partial z}(3z - y) = 2 + 2y + 3 = 5 + 2y \]

Step 2: Apply the Divergence Theorem.

\[ \iint_S \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \iiint_E (5 + 2y)\,dV = 5 \iiint_E dV + 2 \iiint_E y\,dV \]

Step 3: Evaluate using cylindrical geometry and symmetry.
By symmetry across the \(xz\)-plane (since the cylinder \(x^2 + y^2 \le 4\) is symmetric in \(y\)), the odd integral \(\iiint_E y\,dV = 0\).
The volume of the cylinder is \(\text{Vol}(E) = \pi R^2 h = \pi(2^2)(3) = 12\pi\).
Thus:

\[ \iint_S \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = 5(12\pi) + 2(0) = 60\pi \]

body.en:
Green's Theorem Orientation: Green's Theorem \(\oint_C (P\,dx + Q\,dy) = \iint_R (Q_x - P_y)\,dA\) strictly requires a positively oriented (counterclockwise) boundary curve \(C\) keeping the region on the left. If traversing clockwise, you MUST insert a negative sign!

Conservative Vector Fields Checklist: A vector field \(\mathbf{F} = abla f\) has \( ext{curl}(\mathbf{F}) = \mathbf{0}\). On simply connected domains: (1) Path independence \(\int_{C_1} = \int_{C_2}\); (2) Zero work around any closed loop: \(\oint_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = 0\); (3) Fundamental Theorem for Line Integrals: \(\int_C abla f \cdot d\mathbf{r} = f(B) - f(A)\).

Divergence vs Curl: Divergence \( abla \cdot \mathbf{F}\) yields a scalar measuring net outflow; Curl \( abla imes \mathbf{F}\) yields a vector measuring rotational circulation.

Stokes' Theorem Closed Boundary: Stokes' Theorem applies to OPEN surfaces with a boundary curve: \(\oint_C \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{r} = \iint_S ( abla imes \mathbf{F}) \cdot d\mathbf{S}\). If the surface \(S\) is CLOSED (like a complete sphere), it has no boundary curve (\(C = \emptyset\)), so the flux of curl through any closed surface is identically \(0\).

question.en:
Level 3 · Advanced
Use the Divergence Theorem to find the outward flux of \(\mathbf{F} = \langle x^3, y^3, z^3 \rangle\) across the boundary sphere \(S: x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 1\).
question.ar:
Level 3 · Advanced
Use the Divergence Theorem to أوجد outward flux of \(\mathbf{F} = \langle x^3, y^3, z^3 \rangle\) across the boundary sphere \(S: x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = 1\).

solution.en:
Compute the divergence:
\[ \nabla \cdot \mathbf{F} = \frac{\partial}{\partial x}(x^3) + \frac{\partial}{\partial y}(y^3) + \frac{\partial}{\partial z}(z^3) = 3x^2 + 3y^2 + 3z^2 = 3(x^2 + y^2 + z^2) \]
Apply the Divergence Theorem:
\[ \iint_S \mathbf{F} \cdot d\mathbf{S} = \iiint_E 3(x^2 + y^2 + z^2)\,dV \]
Convert to spherical coordinates: \(x^2 + y^2 + z^2 = \rho^2\), \(dV = \rho^2 \sin\phi\,d\rho\,d\phi\,d\theta\):
\[ = 3 \int_0^{2\pi} d\theta \int_0^{\pi} \sin\phi\,d\phi \int_0^1 \rho^2 (\rho^2\,d\rho) = 3(2\pi)(2) \int_0^1 \rho^4\,d\rho = 12\pi \left[ \frac{\rho^5}{5} \right]_0^1 = \frac{12\pi}{5} \]
